data.title: Stocks Bend, but Don't Break, in Head-Spinning September. More Tests Are Coming. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Martin Baccardax

U.S. stocks enter the final throes of September pretty much on pace with the kind of declines expected over the market's historically weakest month, having fought through issues that could have pushed them firmly lower into the close of the third quarter.

A massive surge in Treasury bond yields, which lifted 10-year notes to the highest since 2007, paired with a worrying summer rally in global crude prices that has oil trading firmly north of $100 a barrel, leaned heavily on stocks but didn't tip them over.

A Federal Reserve interest-rate hike, coupled with hawkish language and quickening inflation forecasts, also came and went, with stocks posting their strongest gains in six weeks and an index of the Magnificent Seven tech giants coming within half a point of the all-time high it reached in late May.

Tech stocks, in fact, have largely weathered a series of "end of days" headlines from the AI space, with an index of semiconductor stocks falling around 3.3% over the past month and those in the information technology edging just 1.2% lower despite the torrent of stories tied to apocalyptic AI risks.

Yet through all that, the S&P 500 is down around 0.8% for the month, largely in line with the average September decline since the 1950s, with the Nasdaq Composite holding on to its end of August levels.

The resilience is important heading into a barren three-week stretch for markets, followed by the third quarter earnings season with an update from JPMorgan on Oct. 13, and the potentially game-changing midterm elections on Nov. 3.

"The stock market has held up very well so far in September, but remains on eggshells thanks to rising oil prices and bond yields," said Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments in Raleigh, N.C.

"But we're not out of the woods when it comes to the volatility that typically arises during September and October," he added.

Earnings are likely to provide near-term support, however, with analysts expecting collective S&P 500 profits for the three months ending in September to surge 30% from last year to around $768.8 billion.

That would put the index on pace for a full year gain of around 35%, the strongest since 2021, thanks largely to the tech and AI spending that has powered markets higher since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022.

But can it lean on the faster inflation metrics, and the leg higher analysts are expecting in Treasury yields, into the final months of the year?

Brent crude, the global pricing benchmark for oil, has surged nearly 50% over the past 21/2 months, pushing domestic gas prices nearly 40% higher on the year and taking diesel fuel costs to the highest on record at $6.45 a gallon.

Those elements will wreak havoc on inflation readings over the coming months, with Jeffrey Gundlach, founder of DoubleLine Capital, suggesting CPI readings will soon spike north of 4%.

"The psychology is that inflation is now trending higher," he told CNBC earlier this week, citing inventory buildups in GDP readings and Costco's decision to double the price of its Kirkland branded motor oil. "But I worry that the problem isn't being respected."

Bond markets are clearly concerned, with 10-year yields trending close to the 5% mark on Friday, having pulled back to as low as 4.935% during Thursday's solid equity rally. An increasing number of Wall Street analysts are forecasting higher levels over the coming months.

John Davies, U.S. rate strategist at Standard Chartered, sees 10-year yields hitting 5.5% over the next 12 months, and testing 5.1% by the end of the year, "until the market is more confident that inflation will return to target."

"AI-related investment and issuance, U.S. fiscal concerns, and Japanese repatriation risks remain either active or potential challenges" to the market, he added, "even if the impact of oil prices on yields eventually fades."

Higher rates for longer, alongside a likely change in the composition of the House of Representatives, where Democrats hold a solid lead in polling into the November vote, will pose significant challenges for stocks into the close of the year.

Not everyone agrees, however.

"Equity and bond investors are arguably overreacting" to both the Fed's recent hawkishness and the assumption of faster inflation reading blunting broader markets, said Fundstrat's Tom Lee.

"That 'max hawkish' stance creates a bullish setup for equities," he added, citing the likelihood of softer jobs data, muted inflation readings under a new PCE measuring format, and the lack of concern seen in broader VIX volatility readings, which remain pinned near the lowest levels of the year.

"We think there is a positive setup into month end, and the up move could be very sharply positive," Lee said.

Autumn is approaching, the leaves are about to change and the weather will soon be colder.

Stocks will change, too. But just how much remains to be seen.

Write to Martin Baccardax at martin.baccardax@barrons.com

data.title: Alphabet stock jumps as Wall Street raises targets and search rebounds
data.description:
Wall Street is offering another vote of confidence in Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent firm of Google, which is a key player in advertising, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

Shares climbed in premarket trade after Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney boosted his price objective to $450 from $420, citing new data showing Google's search position has rebounded.

In its most recent poll, Evercore revealed that 78% of respondents said they used Google as their preferred search engine in August. That's up from a low of 70% in 2024 and early 2025.

This change significant because AI-powered search has been one of the major risks that investors have dreaded. Instead, Mahaney said Google's search leadership has improved over the last year and he boosted his expectations for Google's search revenue through 2028.

Now, his sales and operating income estimates for 2028 are 4% to 5% above the Wall Street consensus.

Alphabet also benefited from a Sept. 16 court verdict that fell short of requiring Google to divest its ad-tech division. The corporation has been ordered to adjust its advertising tactics and to allow monitoring for six years.

Tigress Financial also increased its price target to $485 from $415.

The next question is whether increased search use and AI investment can convert into sustainable earnings growth as Alphabet faces stricter scrutiny and higher spending.

data.title: Jungle Camps India appoints Bharat Mandhyan as Lodge Manager at Kanha Jungle Camp
data.description:
Jungle Camps India (JCI) has appointed Bharat Mandhyan as Lodge Manager at Kanha Jungle Camp, bringing three decades of wildlife tourism experience across Kanha, Bandhavgarh and Pench. His experience spans guest services, lodge operations, team management and wildlife experiences.

In his new role, Bharat will oversee the day-to-day functioning of the property, drawing on his experience across guest services, food and beverage, housekeeping, hiring and training, budgeting, inventory and marketing.

Bharat began his career as a naturalist, leading safaris, nature walks and birding excursions, while conducting wildlife lectures and working with forest authorities, drivers and guides on safari operations. He has also contributed to conservation and community initiatives in Bandhavgarh, including socio-economic development programmes, census activities and the development of eco-development plans in coordination with the Forest Department.

Gajendra Singh Rathore, Chairperson & Managing Director, Jungle Camps India, said, “Bharat brings together something that is particularly valuable in wildlife hospitality, a deep understanding of the forest alongside three decades of experience managing lodges and teams. His long association with Kanha and experience across Central India will add significant value to the team at Kanha Jungle Camp.”

data.title: George Verghese Takes Additional Role As MD Of Avante Spaces
data.description:
The appointment adds to Verghese’s existing responsibilities at Kirloskar Industries, where he has served as Managing Director since May 2025.

Avante Spaces Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kirloskar Industries Limited (KIL), has appointed George Verghese as Managing Director, effective 18 September 2026.     Vergheseent will continue until 19 May 2030.

Verghese will take on the role as an additional responsibility alongside his position as Managing Director of KIL, which he has held since 20 May 2025. The appointment is aimed at strengthening leadership across the Kirloskar Group’s businesses.

Commenting on the appointment, Rahul Kirloskar, Chairman, Avante Spaces, said Verghese has been involved with multiple Kirloskar Group companies for more than five years, contributing to business strategy, operational execution, HR, marketing and organisational culture.

“His experience across these areas has added valuable perspective to the Group’s journey, and his expertise will further strengthen Avante Spaces as it builds for the future,” Kirloskar said.

In his role at KIL, Verghese has worked with leadership teams and boards across group companies on strategic direction, operational alignment, institutional strengthening and long-term value creation. He has also contributed to transformation initiatives, organisational effectiveness and enterprise-wide governance practices.

Verghese joined the Kirloskar Group in April 2021 as Vice President – Group HR. He subsequently served as Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO) and Chief of Staff at Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited, where he was part of the core leadership team involved in a strategic business turnaround.

With more than 21 years of leadership experience, Verghese has held roles across global organisations including Dell, Reliance Communications, UST Global and Cummins. His experience spans business operations, human resources, business strategy, marketing and branding.

Verghese holds a Master’s degree in Management from XLRI Jamshedpur and a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering from the College of Engineering, Munnar.

data.title: Nabfid Sanctions Over Rs 3,000 Cr Loans To At Least Four Data Centres
data.description:
Lender sees rising demand for financing as India expands data centre capacity for artificial intelligence infrastructure

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (Nabfid) has sanctioned loans of more than Rs 3,000 crore each to at least four data centre projects as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure grows in India.

The facilities have a moratorium of up to five years, followed by a repayment period of 10 years, Nabfid Managing Director Rajkiran Rai G. said in an interview.

Rai said such projects can generate “good” cash flows despite their long construction periods. Nabfid has also seen demand from hyperscalers, or large cloud service providers, he said.

The financing demand comes as companies increase spending on large data centre projects in India. Global investors including EQT AB, Blackstone and Alphabet, along with Indian conglomerates such as the Adani Group, have committed investments towards data centre and artificial intelligence infrastructure in the country.

Nabfid estimates that India's data centre sector will require about Rs 1 trillion in funding through March 2031, according to a presentation by the lender.

Nabfid Plans Overseas Fundraising

Nabfid is looking to diversify its borrowing sources and has prepared to raise funds through its maiden dollar bond.

The lender plans to raise Rs 1 trillion during the year ending March 2027, with about 40 per cent of the amount expected to come from overseas sources by the end of December, Rai said.

Nabfid has raised close to USD 1 billion through offshore loans under a concessional window provided by the Reserve Bank of India and available until 31 December. It has also mandated foreign banks to mobilise a 10-year dollar bond of a similar amount through the window by the end of September, Rai said.

data.title: Meet India’s 40 Under 40 Sustainability Leaders
data.description:
BW Businessworld debuts India’s first Sustainability 40 Under 40 list, recognising young leaders for measurable impact and innovation

The inaugural BW Sustainability 40 Under 40 list recognises young leaders making a measurable contribution to sustainability through corporate leadership, entrepreneurship, technology, research and advocacy. The Class of 2026 focuses on individual achievement, examining what nominees have changed within their organisations, sectors and communities.

The initiative looks for people who take ownership, develop new approaches and influence action beyond their immediate responsibilities. Its remit covers environmental, social and business outcomes, with attention to both current impact and the potential for future leadership. Innovation encompasses new ideas, technologies and models, while influence includes the ability to inspire action and engage stakeholders.

An Impact-Led Assessment

The debut edition reached more than 300 professionals and attracted over 80 nominations. More than 55 nominations were screened and shortlisted for jury evaluation, spanning corporate, entrepreneurial, academic, research, policy and social impact backgrounds.

The jury process combined nominee presentations with interactions examining their claims, contribution and impact. Assessment covered five parameters, namely sustainability impact, leadership and influence, innovation and originality, reach, influence and adoption, and overall recommendation. Each carried 10 marks, making a maximum score of 50. The process provided for the BW team to consolidate scores, with final selection guided by overall jury assessment and comparative merit.

The Jury

The jury comprised Samir Shah, Managing Partner, Peak Sustainability Venture, and Dr Pradeep Panigrahi, CEO, Sustainability Value Creation LLP. Academic perspectives came from Dr Anirban Ghosh, Head, Centre for Sustainability, Mahindra University, and Dr Padmini Srinivasan, Chairperson, Centre for Corporate Governance and Sustainability, IIM Bangalore.

Members also included Anil Makkar, Group Chief Sustainability Officer, JK Organisation, Nidhi Sarin, Director, Global Energy Alliance for People & Planet, and Prabodha Acharya, Chief Sustainability Officer, JSW. Santosh Jayaram, Adjunct Professor of Practice, Amrita School for Sustainable Futures, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, was also on the panel.

They were joined by Surya Valluri, Chief Sustainability Officer, Grasim Industries, Subrata Basu, General Manager, Environment Sustainability Services, Tata Sustainability Group, and Sudhir Mishra, Managing Partner, Trust Legal. BW Businessworld was represented by Noor Fathima Warsia, Group Editorial Director, and Hoshie Ghaswalla, CEO & Chief Innovation Officer.

The selection framework places the emphasis on what an individual has achieved, influenced or changed. That focus gives the recognition its purpose, identifying people whose contribution can be examined through their work and the outcomes it produces.

data.title: The Leaders Making Sustainability Count
data.description:
The ninth edition of the BW Sustainable World Awards 2026 recognises organisations and individuals advancing climate action, resource stewardship, innovation and responsible business

Climate action, circularity, water conservation and cleaner mobility feature prominently in this year’s roll of honour, alongside sustainability reporting, responsible business and individual leadership. The BW Sustainable World Awards 2026 recognise this work through 40 honours across 16 categories, comprising gold, silver and bronze awards as well as jury mentions.

An initiative of BW Businessworld and BW Sustainability World, the awards seek to identify organisations and individuals demonstrating genuine sustainability impact, leadership, innovation and credibility. The emphasis is on contributions that merit recognition within their respective categories, supported by evidence of meaningful change.

Evaluating The Impact

The 2026 selection process reached more than 500 organisations and received 160 nominations. Of these, 100 were screened and shortlisted for jury evaluation. The evaluation framework set out six parameters including impact, innovation, credibility, scale and relevance, long-term value and category fit. Jurors were asked to consider measurable outcomes, the evidence supporting claims, the potential for wider adoption and the creation of sustained environmental, social or business value. Under the framework, nominees receiving a ‘yes’ verdict progressed to collective jury deliberation to determine gold, silver or bronze recognition.

The Jury Behind The Selection

The jury was chaired by Dr Bhaskar Chatterjee, former Secretary to the Government of India and former Director General of the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs.

Members included Dr Vibha Dhawan of The Energy and Resources Institute, Nisheeth Srivastava of AIA Group, Dr G Sridhar, former Director General of the Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy, sustainability and sustainable finance board advisor Chandni Khosla, Shalini Goyal Bhalla of the International Council for Circular Economy, Sudhir Mishra of Trust Legal, and author, board member and corporate advisor Srinath Sridharan.

The panel also included Chandni Raina of the Ministry of Finance, Dr Ashvini Kumar of Shakti Sustainable Energy Foundation, Dr Sameer Joshi of the Indian Plastics Institute, Shantanu Roy, formaer Chief Sustainability Officer of GAIL, and Shalabh Tandon and Rajesh Miglani of the International Finance Corporation.

Completing the panel were Jatinder Jay Cheema of Chambers of Jay Cheema, Dr Srikanta K Panigrahi of the Indian Institute of Sustainable Development, Nidhi Sarin of the Global Energy Allaiance for People & Planet and Vikram Kotru of FICCI.

data.title: Sebi To Examine Brokers’ Concerns Over New UPI MDR
data.description:
UPI MDR concerns raised by stockbrokers will be examined by SEBI ahead of the new 0.02% charge taking effect on October 15

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will examine concerns raised by stockbrokers over the new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions, with the charge set to take effect from 15 October.

Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator would look into issues raised by the broking community over the impact of the new payment charge. The concerns centre on the possibility that brokers could incur a cost when clients transfer funds into their trading accounts but do not subsequently execute trades.

Under the new framework, UPI transactions linked to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers, dealers and investment advisers will attract an MDR of 0.02 per cent, subject to a maximum charge of Rs 300 per transaction.

Brokers Flag Cost Burden

Brokers have argued that the MDR could create an additional operating cost because the charge is linked to the transfer of funds rather than the revenue generated from a subsequent trade. A client may transfer money to a brokerage account and leave it unused, meaning the broker could incur the UPI cost without earning brokerage revenue.

Brokers have also highlighted the impact of periodic settlement requirements, under which unused client funds are returned and may subsequently be transferred back through UPI.

New-age brokers including Groww, Zerodha, Upstox and Angel One are also preparing representations to Sebi on the proposed MDR structure. Their concerns include the Rs 300 cap and the threshold above which MDR applies.

Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has separately argued that brokers may not be able to absorb the additional cost indefinitely because UPI transfers do not guarantee a corresponding trade or brokerage income.

The capital-market MDR is significantly lower than the 0.4 per cent rate applicable to eligible merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 under the broader UPI framework. Ordinary consumers are not expected to directly bear the MDR on these transactions.

Sebi’s review could determine whether the current structure needs changes for capital-market transactions, particularly where fund transfers do not result in actual investment or trading activity.

The regulator’s examination comes ahead of the implementation date, giving the industry and authorities time to assess the operational and cost implications for brokers.

data.title: Tata Group Stocks Lose $4 Bn As Tata Sons Listing Uncertainty Weighs
data.description:
Tata Chemicals, TCS and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles lead declines as investors react to uncertainty over Tata Sons’ listing and leadership

Tata Group companies lost about USD 4 billion, or Rs 38,361 crore, in combined market value on Friday, as investors reacted to heightened uncertainty over the potential listing and leadership of the conglomerate’s holding company, Tata Sons.

The decline followed the Tata Sons board’s decision on Thursday to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as chairman for another five years and move towards complying with Reserve Bank of India rules that could require the company to list.

The decline came amid a widening dispute between Tata Sons and Tata Trusts, which collectively hold 66 per cent of the holding company. Tata Trusts have opposed a public listing and challenged the validity of the board’s decision to extend Chandrasekaran’s tenure.

Tata Stocks Reverse Gains

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) closed 3.88 per cent lower on Friday, while Tata Chemicals fell 11.04 per cent, its sharpest decline among the major Tata stocks. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles declined 3.4 per cent, while Tata Elxsi fell 3.4 per cent and Tata Investment Corporation lost 2.55 per cent.

Tata Steel also declined 0.93 per cent. However, the movement was not uniform across the group, with Tata Capital gaining 2.42 per cent, Tata Power rising 1.57 per cent and Tata Motors advancing 1.56 per cent.

The Friday declines reversed part of the gains recorded by several Tata stocks on Thursday after the company announced Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and its decision to initiate steps towards compliance with the RBI’s regulatory requirements.

Reuters calculations based on exchange data showed that the combined market value of listed Tata Group companies stood at about USD 268.5 billion at Thursday’s close and before Friday's decline.

Listing Dispute Deepens

The market reaction comes as Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board take different positions on the future ownership structure of the group’s holding company.

Tata Trusts said they had not agreed to the listing and that all available options should be examined following the RBI’s 11 September communication.

The Trusts have also maintained that Tata Sons should remain unlisted, pointing to a unanimous board decision in March 2024 and resolutions passed by the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust in July 2025.

The latest developments have also brought the Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s 18.4 per cent stake in Tata Sons into focus.

The group has proposed monetising part of its holding through a two-tranche transaction that would generate at least USD 2.61 billion, or about Rs 25,000 crore, over 18 months.

Leadership Adds To Uncertainty

Alongside the listing dispute, investors are also assessing the implications of the disagreement over Chandrasekaran’s tenure. The Tata Sons board approved his reappointment for another five years on Thursday.

Tata Trusts have challenged the validity of the resolution, saying Noel Tata’s vote against the proposal meant it was a “legal nullity” under the company’s Articles.

data.title: Indian Shares End Sixth Straight Week Lower As Oil, Rate Fears Weigh
data.description:
The Nifty 50 rose 0.33 per cent to close at 23,346.40 on Friday, while the Sensex slipped 0.03 per cent to 74,294.96

Indian shares recorded their sixth consecutive weekly decline on Friday, marking their longest losing streak since 2020, as crude oil prices above $100 a barrel and concerns over global interest rates weighed on investor sentiment.

The Nifty 50 rose 0.33 per cent to close at 23,346.40 on Friday, while the Sensex slipped 0.03 per cent to 74,294.96. Despite the mixed session, both benchmarks ended the week lower, with the Nifty declining 0.22 per cent and the Sensex losing 0.65 per cent.

A decline in oil prices during the session and bargain buying following recent losses provided some support to equities. However, weakness in information technology and Tata Group stocks, along with strong demand for domestic initial public offerings (IPOs), continued to weigh on the broader market.

The $2.3 billion NSE IPO was fully subscribed on its second day of bidding, highlighting strong demand for primary-market offerings. However, the flow of money into IPOs also reduced liquidity available for the secondary market.

“While markets gained during the session, the move appears to be driven largely by bargain buying after the recent oversold conditions, rather than signalling a meaningful reversal in sentiment,” said Saurabh Jain, Deputy Vice President of Equities at SMC Global.

Jain said uncertainty over a near-term resolution to tensions in the Middle East continued to pressure Indian equities because of the country's exposure to crude oil prices. He also pointed to elevated global bond yields and persistently high US interest rates as factors reducing the relative appeal of emerging markets such as India for foreign investors.

The weakness was broad-based during the week, with 10 of the 16 major sectors recording losses. The broader market also remained under pressure, with the small-cap Nifty Smallcap 100 falling 0.15 per cent and the Nifty Midcap 100 declining 0.01 per cent on the week.

Insurance stocks were among the notable gainers. HDFC Life rose 4 per cent and SBI Life gained 2.8 per cent as investors responded positively to the sector's growth outlook and increased transparency associated with the transition in financial reporting.

Systematix Research expects the new accounting framework to provide a more granular view of underlying profitability in the insurance sector.

Tata Group stocks, meanwhile, faced significant selling pressure. TCS, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Investment and Tata Chemicals fell between 2.5 per cent and 11.1 per cent during the week.

The selling came amid heightened uncertainty surrounding the potential listing and leadership of Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata Group, following a public dispute.

The market's six-week losing streak comes as investors navigate a combination of geopolitical uncertainty, elevated crude prices, tighter global financial conditions and continued foreign-investor concerns.
